scientific_hypothesis: A 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with non-quarter-wave thickness tuning can achieve simultaneous high transmittance in 1530-1565 nm and high reflectance in 400-700 nm, with optimization convergence indicated by diminishing score improvement while thickness variance stabilizes.
expected_advantages: Maintaining exact 24-layer topology allows direct comparison with iteration 05 results
Gradient optimization with variance monitoring provides convergence diagnostics
15% step-size reduction near convergence probes local optimum without destabilizing band-edge alignments
Control arm isolates the effect of thickness tuning from material or topology changes
known_risks: Uncertain: Exact refractive index values of hfo2 and sio2 at 400 nm vs 1550 nm - would need material_catalog data to confirm dispersion
Uncertain: Whether 24 layers is optimal vs 20, 26, or 28 layers - this route does not explore layer count as a variable
Uncertain: Whether starting with HfO2 (high-index) vs SiO2 (low-index) at the air interface is optimal for this dual-band requirement
Uncertain: The 5 nm variance threshold and 1e-4 score improvement threshold are recalled heuristics, not validated for this specific problem
Uncertain: Fused silica substrate refractive index matching - assumed to be ~1.45 at 1550 nm but exact value from catalog needed
expected_observations: best_target_score should show diminishing improvement across rounds (convergence pattern)
tightest_margin should remain stable or improve slightly as optimization refines
thicknesses_nm per-layer standard deviation should decrease as optimization converges
valid_candidates count should remain high (physical validity maintained)
If variance exceeds 5 nm while score improvement drops below 1e-4, step-size reduction should stabilize thickness values without degrading target score
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-4 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates drops below 3 for two consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds by 10% and continue
If per-layer thickness standard deviation falls below 1 nm across all layers for three consecutive rounds, consider convergence achieved and stop
After 5 optimization rounds complete, stop and retain the best candidate from all rounds
